questions.question: Which input attribute must match the label's 'for' attribute for explicit accessible pairing?
questions.explanation: The 'for' attribute of a <label> must match the 'id' attribute of the corresponding input element.

questions.question: What is the primary accessibility drawback of relying on placeholder text instead of a <label>?
options: Placeholders disappear once a user types, disorienting users and impairing screen readers
Placeholders are not rendered in Chrome
questions.hint: What happens when you type into a placeholder?
questions.explanation: Placeholder text disappears as soon as typing begins and has poor color contrast, making it an inaccessible substitute for labels.

questions.question: Which element acts as the accessible caption header for a <fieldset>?
questions.explanation: <legend> is the semantic caption element for <fieldset>.

questions.question: What happens when a user clicks on the text inside a properly linked <label>?
options: The associated input element gains focus or toggles state
questions.hint: It activates the linked form control.
questions.explanation: Clicking a properly linked label focuses text inputs and toggles checkboxes and radio buttons.

questions.question: Which semantic element is recommended for grouping related payment options like Credit Card, PayPal, and Apple Pay?
questions.explanation: <fieldset> semantically groups related controls within a web form.
